chunks.section: BIS Certification & Schemes — Initial Ingestion Notes
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS public information.

Official source: https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/product-certification-process/ The current BIS page lists official material for: - Scheme-I of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 — product certification for use of the ISI mark. - Guidelines for Grant of Licence. - Additional Guidelines for Scheme-I. - Guidelines for dealing with product non-conformity. - Guidelines for dealing with unsatisfactory performance. - Guidelines for change in scope of licence. - Guidelines for renewal of licence. - Guidelines for retesting of samples. - Guidelines for factory surveillance. - Guidelines for market surveillance. - Guidelines for utilisation of Cluster Based Test Facility (CBTF) by MSMEs. - Scheme-IV of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 and related guidance.

Official source: https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/ Use this source for current information about products covered by compulsory certification / Quality Control Orders and the applicable conformity-assessment scheme.
Preserve the official source URL and retrieval date in the knowledge metadata. Do not infer current fees, dates, product applicability, or scheme requirements from model knowledge.
Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/product-certification-faq/?lang=en Application Portal: https://www.manakonline.in

chunks.section: Product Certification Process & Grant of Licence
chunks.chunk_text: - Scheme Overview: BIS operates Product Certification Scheme (Scheme-I) under BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 for grant of licence to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). - Online Application: Manufacturers must register and apply through the official Manakonline e-portal (manakonline.in) along with application fee and required documents. - Infrastructure Prerequisites: The manufacturing unit must have necessary manufacturing machinery, complete in-house testing facilities as per Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT), and qualified technical quality control personnel.

chunks.section: Certification Pathways: Normal vs Simplified Procedure
chunks.chunk_text: 1. Normal Procedure (Option 1): - Preliminary factory audit conducted by BIS officers. - Verification of manufacturing infrastructure, quality control system, and in-house testing laboratory. - Drawing of official verification samples during audit for testing in BIS recognized laboratory. - Grant of CM/L (Certification Mark Licence) upon receiving passing test reports and compliance with SIT. 2. Simplified Procedure (Option 2): - Available for select products where applicant gets sample pre-tested from a BIS-recognized testing laboratory. - Application submitted with pre-testing report, factory layout, and manufacturing details. - Licence granted after verification of application documents and factory audit, reducing grant timeline.

- Once granted, licence is valid for 1 to 2 years and renewable upon payment of marking fees. - Licensees must follow the prescribed Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT) and maintain routine test records. - BIS conducts unannounced periodic factory surveillance audits and draws market surveillance samples from retail channels to ensure continuous compliance. - Misuse of ISI mark or selling non-conforming goods is a cognizable offense under Section 29 of the BIS Act, 2016.

chunks.section: BIS Hallmarking & HUID — Initial Ingestion Notes
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS public information.

https://www.bis.gov.in/hallmarking-overview/hallmarking-faqs/hallmarking-faq/ Current official FAQ facts to index: - HUID means Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number. - HUID is a six-digit alphanumeric number and is unique for each hallmarked item. - Consumers can verify HUID using the BIS Care App's "Verify HUID" feature. - BIS states that, since the introduction of HUID on 1 July 2021, hallmark on gold jewellery consists of three marks: BIS logo, purity of the article in caratage and fineness, and six-digit alphanumeric HUID number.

https://www.bis.gov.in/hallmarking-overview/consumer-protection/?lang=en BIS states that: - Consumers can have jewellery/sample tested at BIS Recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centres on a chargeable basis. - BIS provides guidance concerning testing and compensation in cases where hallmarked jewellery is found to have lower purity than declared. - HUID authenticity can be checked through the BIS Care App.

chunks.section: The 3 Mandatory Hallmarks on Gold Jewellery
chunks.chunk_text: Since 1 July 2021, hallmark on gold jewellery consists of three mandatory marks: 1. BIS Logo (Triangle Hallmark). 2. Purity of the article in Caratage & Fineness (24K999, 23K958, 22K916, 20K833, 18K750, 14K585). 3. 6-digit Alphanumeric HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) code unique to each piece.

- HUID is a 6-digit unique alphanumeric code laser-inscribed on each item at BIS-recognized Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs). - The HUID links the item in the central BIS digital registry to the manufacturing jeweller, the AHC that tested it, date of hallmarking, and exact purity grade. - Violations, sale of fake hallmarks, or selling unhallmarked gold in mandatory districts attract penalties under Section 29 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016.

Verify Licence Details (CM/L): Enter the 7-digit or 8-digit CM/L license number displayed on any ISI-marked product to check validity, manufacturer name, brand name, address, and applicable Indian Standard. 2. Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/system-certification-overview/systems-under-certification/?lang=en

The Bureau of Indian Standards operates management systems certification schemes for organizations across multiple industrial and service sectors. These certifications demonstrate compliance with international standards: 1. Quality Management System (QMS) — IS/ISO 9001: Demonstrates consistent ability to provide products and services that meet customer and applicable statutory requirements. 2. Environmental Management System (EMS) — IS/ISO 14001: Provides a framework for protecting the environment and responding to changing environmental conditions. 3. Food Safety Management System (FSMS) — IS/ISO 22000: Ensures food safety throughout the food chain up to the point of consumption. 4. Occupational Health and Safety Management System (OHSMS) — IS/ISO 45001: Improves workplace safety and reduces employee risks. 5. Information Security Management System (ISMS) — IS/ISO/IEC 27001: Secures organizational information assets and data confidentiality. 6. Energy Management System (EnMS) — IS/ISO 50001: Enables organizations to establish systems and processes to improve energy efficiency. 7. Medical Devices Quality Management System (MDQMS) — IS/ISO 13485: Specific requirements for regulatory compliance of medical device manufacturers.

- Application: Submission of organization profile, system manual, and applicable standard. - Stage 1 Audit: Off-site and on-site review of management system documentation, adequacy of policies, and readiness for Stage 2. - Stage 2 Audit: Comprehensive on-site audit evaluating implementation, operational control, and effectiveness of the management system. - Certification Decision: Grant of license upon satisfactory resolution of non-conformities (NCs). - Surveillance & Recertification: Periodic surveillance audits conducted every year, with complete recertification every 3 years.

chunks.section: BIS Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) FAQ
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/fmcs/fmcs-faqs/?lang=en

- Scheme Basis: FMCS operates under Scheme-I of Schedule-II of the Bureau of Indian Standards (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. - Purpose: Grants licence to foreign manufacturers located outside India to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on products exported to the Indian market. - Scope: Covers both voluntary standards and products notified under Compulsory Quality Control Orders (QCOs) by Government of India ministries.

1. Authorized Indian Representative (AIR): - Every foreign applicant must nominate an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) who is an Indian resident or an entity incorporated in India. - The AIR is legally responsible for compliance with the BIS Act, 2016, rules, regulations, and terms of the license agreement. 2. In-house Manufacturing & Testing Facility: - The foreign manufacturing unit must have independent manufacturing facilities and complete testing equipment as per the relevant Indian Standard. 3. Factory Audit by BIS Officers: - BIS technical officers visit the manufacturing premises abroad to audit manufacturing infrastructure, test facilities, quality control systems, and draw verification samples. 4. Independent Testing in India: - Verification samples drawn during the foreign factory inspection are tested in BIS recognized laboratories in India. 5. Financial Compliance: - Upon successful verification, the foreign manufacturer must submit a Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG) and pay applicable marking fees prior to license grant.

chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/scheme-ii-registration-scheme/?lang=en CRS Portal: https://www.crsbis.in/BIS/

chunks.chunk_text: - Unlike Scheme-I (ISI Mark), Scheme-II does NOT require an on-site factory audit prior to registration. - Testing Requirement: The manufacturer gets product models tested in a BIS-recognized testing laboratory located in India. - Test Report Validity: Test reports submitted for registration must not be older than 90 days from the date of issue. - Grant of Registration: Upon online submission of valid test report, undertaking of compliance, and fee, BIS issues a unique Registration Number.

Laboratory Testing: Drawn samples are tested against relevant Indian Standard specifications in a BIS-approved laboratory. 4. Grant of CoC: A Certificate of Conformity is issued strictly covering the verified batch quantity upon passing laboratory tests.

1. Product Testing: Comprehensive type-testing of product prototypes at BIS recognized or accredited testing laboratories. 2. chunks.section: Product Certification Process & Grant of Licence
chunks.chunk_text: - Scheme Overview: BIS operates Product Certification Scheme (Scheme-I) under BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 for grant of licence to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). - Online Application: Manufacturers must register and apply through the official Manakonline e-portal (manakonline.in) along with application fee and required documents. - Infrastructure Prerequisites: The manufacturing unit must have necessary manufacturing machinery, complete in-house testing facilities as per Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT), and qualified technical quality control personnel.

chunks.section: Certification Pathways: Normal vs Simplified Procedure
chunks.chunk_text: 1. Normal Procedure (Option 1): - Preliminary factory audit conducted by BIS officers. - Verification of manufacturing infrastructure, quality control system, and in-house testing laboratory. - Drawing of official verification samples during audit for testing in BIS recognized laboratory. - Grant of CM/L (Certification Mark Licence) upon receiving passing test reports and compliance with SIT. 2. Simplified Procedure (Option 2): - Available for select products where applicant gets sample pre-tested from a BIS-recognized testing laboratory. - Application submitted with pre-testing report, factory layout, and manufacturing details. - Licence granted after verification of application documents and factory audit, reducing grant timeline.

- Once granted, licence is valid for 1 to 2 years and renewable upon payment of marking fees. - Licensees must follow the prescribed Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT) and maintain routine test records. - BIS conducts unannounced periodic factory surveillance audits and draws market surveillance samples from retail channels to ensure continuous compliance. - Misuse of ISI mark or selling non-conforming goods is a cognizable offense under Section 29 of the BIS Act, 2016.

Scheme-X License: Grant of certificate allowing the application of Scheme-X Standard Mark for the certified industrial equipment series.
Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/system-certification-overview/systems-under-certification/?lang=en

The Bureau of Indian Standards operates management systems certification schemes for organizations across multiple industrial and service sectors. These certifications demonstrate compliance with international standards: 1. Quality Management System (QMS) — IS/ISO 9001: Demonstrates consistent ability to provide products and services that meet customer and applicable statutory requirements. 2. Environmental Management System (EMS) — IS/ISO 14001: Provides a framework for protecting the environment and responding to changing environmental conditions. 3. Food Safety Management System (FSMS) — IS/ISO 22000: Ensures food safety throughout the food chain up to the point of consumption. 4. Occupational Health and Safety Management System (OHSMS) — IS/ISO 45001: Improves workplace safety and reduces employee risks. 5. Information Security Management System (ISMS) — IS/ISO/IEC 27001: Secures organizational information assets and data confidentiality. 6. Energy Management System (EnMS) — IS/ISO 50001: Enables organizations to establish systems and processes to improve energy efficiency. 7. Medical Devices Quality Management System (MDQMS) — IS/ISO 13485: Specific requirements for regulatory compliance of medical device manufacturers.

- Application: Submission of organization profile, system manual, and applicable standard. - Stage 1 Audit: Off-site and on-site review of management system documentation, adequacy of policies, and readiness for Stage 2. - Stage 2 Audit: Comprehensive on-site audit evaluating implementation, operational control, and effectiveness of the management system. - Certification Decision: Grant of license upon satisfactory resolution of non-conformities (NCs). - Surveillance & Recertification: Periodic surveillance audits conducted every year, with complete recertification every 3 years.

chunks.section_title: Official Quality Control Orders (QCO) Compendium — Bureau of Indian Standards
chunks.content: # Official Quality Control Orders (QCO) Compendium — Bureau of Indian Standards

Under Section 16 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016, the Central Government, after consulting the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), notifies Quality Control Orders (QCOs) in the Gazette of India. Once a product is notified under a QCO: 1. It becomes mandatory for every domestic manufacturer and overseas manufacturer exporting to India to conform to the specified Indian Standard (IS). 2. The product MUST bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark under Scheme I, or CRS Registration Mark under Scheme II) under a valid licence/certificate from BIS. 3. No person, distributor, retailer, importer, or e-commerce entity shall manufacture, import, store, sell, or distribute goods that do not comply with the notified standard.

chunks.section_title: Statutory Framework & Enforcement under Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016
chunks.content: # Statutory Framework & Enforcement under Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is the National Standards Body of India established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 (Act No. 11 of 2016), replacing the predecessor 1986 Act.

### Section 16 — Mandatory Use of Standard Mark (QCOs) The Central Government, if satisfied that it is necessary or expedient so to do in the public interest or for the protection of human, animal or plant health, safety of the environment, or prevention of unfair trade practices, or national security, may direct that any goods or article of any specified industry, process, system or service shall conform to the Indian Standard and direct the use of the Standard Mark under a license or certificate of conformity. ### Section 17 — Prohibition on Improper Use of Standard Mark No person shall use in relation to any article, goods, process, system or service, or in any title, trade mark or design the Standard Mark or any colorable imitation thereof, except under a valid licence or certificate of conformity granted by the Bureau. ### Section 29 — Strict Criminal & Civil Penalties for Violation 1. Violation of Section 16 (manufacturing, importing, storing, selling, or offering for sale non-compliant mandatory goods): - **Imprisonment**: Term which may extend up to two (2) years. - **Monetary Fine**: Fine which shall not be less than ₹2,00,000 (two lakh rupees) and which may extend up to ₹5,00,000 (five lakh rupees) for the first violation, or up to ten (10) times the value of the goods produced, sold, or offered for sale. - For second or subsequent offenses: Fine not less than ₹5,00,000 and imprisonment up to two

(five lakh rupees) for the first violation, or up to ten (10) times the value of the goods produced, sold, or offered for sale. - For second or subsequent offenses: Fine not less than ₹5,00,000 and imprisonment up to two years. 2. Violation of Section 17 (unauthorized use of ISI Mark or false hallmarking): - Imprisonment up to one year and fine not less than ₹1,00,000 up to ₹5,00,000. ### Section 30 — Offenses by Companies Where an offense under this Act has been committed by a company, every person who at the time the offense was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company itself, shall be deemed guilty of the offense and liable to be proceeded against. ### Section 49 — Consumer Redressal & Statutory Compensation Where an article marked with the Standard Mark does not conform to the relevant Indian Standard, the consumer or purchaser is entitled to: 1. Replacement of the non-conforming article with a conforming one. 2. Refund of the price paid. 3. In case of precious metal articles (hallmarked gold/silver): If the purity is found below the declared fineness grade, the consumer is legally entitled to compensation from the hallmarked jeweller equal to **two times (2x) the difference in purity value** calculated at the prevailing market price of the metal on the date of purchase.

1. **Normal Procedure (Option 1)**: Factory audit by BIS inspecting officer followed by drawing of sample for testing in an independent laboratory. Licence granted within 60-90 days upon conformity. 2. **Simplified Procedure (Option 2)**: For domestic manufacturers where an in-house laboratory is established and complete test report from a BIS-recognized/NABL-accredited laboratory is submitted. Licence granted within 30 days after initial verification. 3. **MSME & Start-up Concessions**: - Micro enterprises: 20% concession on minimum marking fee. - Small enterprises: 20% concession on minimum marking fee. - Women entrepreneurs & Recognized Start-ups: 50% concession on minimum marking fee for the grant of initial license.

chunks.section_title: Mandatory Food Safety and BIS Certification Products (FSSAI & BIS Co-Regulation)
chunks.content: # Mandatory Food Safety and BIS Certification Products (FSSAI & BIS Co-Regulation)

Under Regulation 2.3.14 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011, issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, read with the BIS Act, 2016: No person or food business operator shall manufacture, sell, or exhibit for sale any of the specified food and beverage items except under the BIS Certification Mark (ISI Mark).

### 1. Packaged Drinking Water - **IS 14543:2024**: Packaged Drinking Water (Other than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) — Specification. - Mandatory for all commercial 20-litre jars, 1-litre bottles, pouches, and containers. - Factory must have an in-house dedicated testing laboratory equipped for physical, chemical, and microbiological parameters (Total Viable Count, Coliforms, E. coli, Salmonella, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Yeast & Mould). - Source water must be tested for toxic heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury) and pesticide residues (organochlorines, organophosphorus). ### 2. Packaged Natural Mineral Water - **IS 13428:2024**: Packaged Natural Mineral Water — Specification. - Must be obtained directly from natural subterranean sources (springs, artesian wells) without alteration of mineral composition. ### 3. Infant Nutrition & Milk Products - **IS 1165:2002**: Milk powder. - **IS 14433:2007**: Infant milk substitutes, milk-based and cereal-based foods. - **IS 11536:2007**: Processed cereal-based complementary foods for infants. - **IS 4812:2014**: Condensed milk, partly skimmed and skimmed condensed milk. ### Statutory Enforcement Under the joint enforcement framework of FSSAI and BIS, running a packaged drinking water plant without a valid BIS licence (CM/L number) and FSSAI licence is an illegal operation subject to immediate factory sealing, seizure of packaged stock, and criminal prosecution.

- **IS 4151:2015**: Protective Helmets for Two-Wheeler Riders. Compulsory under Helmet (Quality Control) Order. Mandatory shock absorption, penetration resistance, and chinstrap retention tests. - **IS 2553 (Part 2)**: Safety Glass for Road Transport (windshields, side/rear windows). - **IS 15633 & IS 15636**: Automotive Pneumatic Tyres for Passenger Cars and Commercial Vehicles.

chunks.section: Statutory Framework & Enforcement under Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016
chunks.chunk_text: # Statutory Framework & Enforcement under Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is the National Standards Body of India established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 (Act No. 11 of 2016), replacing the predecessor 1986 Act.

### Section 16 — Mandatory Use of Standard Mark (QCOs) The Central Government, if satisfied that it is necessary or expedient so to do in the public interest or for the protection of human, animal or plant health, safety of the environment, or prevention of unfair trade practices, or national security, may direct that any goods or article of any specified industry, process, system or service shall conform to the Indian Standard and direct the use of the Standard Mark under a license or certificate of conformity. ### Section 17 — Prohibition on Improper Use of Standard Mark No person shall use in relation to any article, goods, process, system or service, or in any title, trade mark or design the Standard Mark or any colorable imitation thereof, except under a valid licence or certificate of conformity granted by the Bureau. ### Section 29 — Strict Criminal & Civil Penalties for Violation 1. Violation of Section 16 (manufacturing, importing, storing, selling, or offering for sale non-compliant mandatory goods): - **Imprisonment**: Term which may extend up to two (2) years. - **Monetary Fine**: Fine which shall not be less than ₹2,00,000 (two lakh rupees) and which may extend up to ₹5,00,000 (five lakh rupees) for the first violation, or up to ten (10) times the value of the goods produced, sold,

**Monetary Fine**: Fine which shall not be less than ₹2,00,000 (two lakh rupees) and which may extend up to ₹5,00,000 (five lakh rupees) for the first violation, or up to ten (10) times the value of the goods produced, sold, or offered for sale. - For second or subsequent offenses: Fine not less than ₹5,00,000 and imprisonment up to two years. 2. Violation of Section 17 (unauthorized use of ISI Mark or false hallmarking): - Imprisonment up to one year and fine not less than ₹1,00,000 up to ₹5,00,000. ### Section 30 — Offenses by Companies Where an offense under this Act has been committed by a company, every person who at the time the offense was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company itself, shall be deemed guilty of the offense and liable to be proceeded against. ### Section 49 — Consumer Redressal & Statutory Compensation Where an article marked with the Standard Mark does not conform to the relevant Indian Standard, the consumer or purchaser is entitled to: 1. Replacement of the non-conforming article with a conforming one. 2. Refund of the price paid. 3. In case of precious metal articles (hallmarked gold/silver): If the purity is found below the

Standard, the consumer or purchaser is entitled to: 1. Replacement of the non-conforming article with a conforming one. 2. Refund of the price paid. 3. In case of precious metal articles (hallmarked gold/silver): If the purity is found below the declared fineness grade, the consumer is legally entitled to compensation from the hallmarked jeweller equal to **two times (2x) the difference in purity value** calculated at the prevailing market price of the metal on the date of purchase.

1. **Normal Procedure (Option 1)**: Factory audit by BIS inspecting officer followed by drawing of sample for testing in an independent laboratory. Licence granted within 60-90 days upon conformity. 2. **Simplified Procedure (Option 2)**: For domestic manufacturers where an in-house laboratory is established and complete test report from a BIS-recognized/NABL-accredited laboratory is submitted. Licence granted within 30 days after initial verification. 3. **MSME & Start-up Concessions**: - Micro enterprises: 20% concession on minimum marking fee. - Small enterprises: 20% concession on minimum marking fee. - Women entrepreneurs & Recognized Start-ups: 50% concession on minimum marking fee for the grant of initial license.

chunks.section: Mandatory Food Safety and BIS Certification Products (FSSAI & BIS Co-Regulation)
chunks.chunk_text: # Mandatory Food Safety and BIS Certification Products (FSSAI & BIS Co-Regulation)

Under Regulation 2.3.14 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011, issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, read with the BIS Act, 2016: No person or food business operator shall manufacture, sell, or exhibit for sale any of the specified food and beverage items except under the BIS Certification Mark (ISI Mark).

### 1. Packaged Drinking Water - **IS 14543:2024**: Packaged Drinking Water (Other than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) — Specification. - Mandatory for all commercial 20-litre jars, 1-litre bottles, pouches, and containers. - Factory must have an in-house dedicated testing laboratory equipped for physical, chemical, and microbiological parameters (Total Viable Count, Coliforms, E. coli, Salmonella, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Yeast & Mould). - Source water must be tested for toxic heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury) and pesticide residues (organochlorines, organophosphorus). ### 2. Packaged Natural Mineral Water - **IS 13428:2024**: Packaged Natural Mineral Water — Specification. - Must be obtained directly from natural subterranean sources (springs, artesian wells) without alteration of mineral composition. ### 3. Infant Nutrition & Milk Products - **IS 1165:2002**: Milk powder. - **IS 14433:2007**: Infant milk substitutes, milk-based and cereal-based foods. - **IS 11536:2007**: Processed cereal-based complementary foods for infants. - **IS 4812:2014**: Condensed milk, partly skimmed and skimmed condensed milk. ### Statutory Enforcement Under the joint enforcement framework of FSSAI and BIS, running a packaged drinking water plant without a valid BIS licence (CM/L number) and FSSAI licence is an illegal operation subject to immediate factory sealing, seizure of packaged stock, and criminal prosecution.

chunks.section: Electrical Appliances — Indian Standards and QCO Compulsory Certification
chunks.chunk_text: # Electrical Appliances — Indian Standards and QCO Compulsory Certification

The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) mandates compulsory certification for numerous electrical appliances under Scheme I (ISI Mark). The Electrical Equipment (Quality Control) Orders issued by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) require that specified electrical products conform to designated Indian Standards before manufacture, sale, import, or distribution in India.

### Wiring and Cables - **IS 694:2010**: PVC Insulated Cables for working voltages up to and including 1100 V. Compulsory under Scheme I (ISI Mark). Covers single-core, multi-core, flexible, and flat cables for domestic and industrial wiring installations. - **IS 10810 (Part 1):1984/ISO 6722**: Insulated cables for automobiles — Requirements and test methods. - **IS 1554 (Part 1):2022**: PVC Insulated (Heavy Duty) Electric Cables for voltages up to and including 1100V. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 7098 (Part 1):2020**: Cross-linked Polyethylene Insulated PVC Sheathed Cables for voltages up to and including 1100V. Compulsory under Scheme I. ### Switches and Sockets - **IS 3854:1997**: Switches for domestic and similar purposes. Compulsory under Scheme I. Covers single-pole, two-pole, and three-pole switches rated up to 16 A, 250 V. - **IS 1293:2019**: Plugs, Socket-Outlets and Socket-Outlet Adaptors for Domestic and Similar Purposes. Compulsory under Scheme I. Covers 6 A and 16 A rated plugs and sockets. ### Fans - **IS 374:2019**: Ceiling Fans — Specification. Compulsory under Scheme I. Covers sweep sizes 600 mm to 1400 mm. Mandatory testing includes air delivery, service value, power consumption, and safety. ### Electric Irons - **IS 302 (Part 2, Section 3):2008**: Electric Irons — Safety requirements. Compulsory under Scheme I. Applies to electric irons for household or similar purposes. ### Water Heaters and Geysers - **IS 302 (Part 2, Section 21):2009**: Storage Water Heaters. Compulsory under Scheme I. Covers immersion-type and storage-type water heaters for domestic use. Mandatory tests include electrical safety, thermal cut-off, and earth continuity. ### LED and Lighting - **IS 10322 (Part 5/Section 1):2013**: Luminaires — General Requirements and Tests. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 16102 (Part 1):2012**: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services — Safety. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 16102 (Part 2):2012**: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps — Performance

5/Section 1):2013**: Luminaires — General Requirements and Tests. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 16102 (Part 1):2012**: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services — Safety. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 16102 (Part 2):2012**: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps — Performance Requirements. Compulsory under Scheme I. ### MCBs and Switchgear - **IS 8828:2018**: Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs) for rated voltages not exceeding 253V. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS/IEC 60947-2:2016**: Low-Voltage Switchgear and Controlgear — Circuit Breakers.

All electrical appliances under compulsory certification must undergo: 1. Type testing at a BIS-recognized laboratory 2. Factory inspection by BIS officers 3. Periodic surveillance and sample testing 4. Marking compliance (Standard Mark / ISI Mark on product and packaging) Source: Bureau of Indian Standards — https://www.bis.gov.in/ Source: Scheme I Guidelines — https://www.bis.gov.in/index.php/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/ Category: Electrical Appliances

chunks.section: Food Safety Standards — Indian Standards, FSSAI, and BIS Compulsory Certificatio
chunks.chunk_text: # Food Safety Standards — Indian Standards, FSSAI, and BIS Compulsory Certification

Food safety in India is regulated jointly by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) and the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Several food product standards are mandated under BIS Scheme I (ISI Mark) by Quality Control Orders. FSSAI references Indian Standards in its Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations.

- **IS 14543:2024**: Packaged Drinking Water (Other than Packaged Natural Mineral Water). Compulsory under BIS Scheme I. Specifies requirements for microbiological, chemical, and physical quality parameters. All manufacturers must have BIS licence and display ISI Mark. Mandatory factory-level in-house testing laboratory. - **IS 13428:2024**: Packaged Natural Mineral Water. Compulsory under BIS Scheme I. Covers spring water, artesian well water, and other natural mineral water sources. Requires source-specific mineral analysis.

- **IS 1165:2016**: Milk Powder — Whole and Skim. Referenced by FSSAI. Specifies fat content, moisture, acidity, and microbiological limits. - **IS 1166:2017**: Condensed Milk (Sweetened and Unsweetened). Referenced by FSSAI regulations. - **IS 5765 (Part 1):2010**: Infant Milk Food based on cow or buffalo milk. Referenced by FSSAI. Mandatory testing for protein, fat, moisture, and contaminant limits.

- **IS 548 (Part 1):2023**: Methods of sampling and test for oils and fats. Foundational standard used across all edible oil testing. - **IS 3657**: Mustard Oil (3rd Revision). Referenced by FSSAI. - **IS 8322**: Blended Edible Vegetable Oils. Referenced by FSSAI for blended oil standards.

- **IS 4333 (Part 1)**: Methods of Analysis of Foodgrains — Physical examination. - **IS 4333 (Part 2)**: Methods of Analysis of Foodgrains — Determination of moisture content. - **IS 7419**: Wheat Flour (Atta, Maida, Suji, Sooji).

- **IS 10146:2011**: Polyethylene for its Safe Use in Contact with Foodstuffs, Pharmaceuticals and Drinking Water. Compulsory under QCO. - **IS 10142:1999**: Polypropylene and its copolymers for safe use in contact with foodstuffs. Compulsory. - **IS 10151:1999**: PVC and its copolymers for safe use in contact with foodstuffs. Compulsory. - **IS 15495:2020**: Water-based food-grade greases.

- **IS 1797:2005**: Ground Black Pepper (Kali Mirch). - **IS 7318:2005**: Turmeric (Haldi) Powder — Specification. - **IS 8933**: Chilli Powder — Specification. - **IS 2105**: Red Chillies, Whole — Specification.

BIS-certified food products must undergo: 1. Physical testing (moisture, foreign matter) 2. Chemical testing (pH, acidity, pesticide residues, heavy metals) 3. Microbiological testing (total plate count, E. coli, coliform, yeast, mould) 4. Sensory evaluation (taste, odour, appearance) 5. Packaging compliance (migration limits for food-contact materials) Testing must be done at BIS-recognized / NABL-accredited laboratories. Source: Bureau of Indian Standards — https://www.bis.gov.in/ Source: FSSAI — https://www.fssai.gov.in/ Source: Standards / Know Your Standard — https://standards.bis.gov.in/ Category: Food and Consumer Products

chunks.section: Electronics and IT Goods — Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II)
chunks.chunk_text: # Electronics and IT Goods — Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II)

The Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS), also called BIS Scheme II, requires that specified electronics and IT products be registered with BIS before they can be manufactured, imported, sold, or distributed in India. CRS is administered by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). Unlike Scheme I (ISI Mark), CRS does not require BIS factory inspection; instead, products must be tested at a BIS-recognized laboratory and registration is granted based on test reports.

1. **Application**: Manufacturer/importer applies online via BIS portal (manakonline.in) 2. **Testing**: Product samples sent to a BIS-recognized lab for testing against the specified Indian Standard 3. **Test Report**: Lab submits test report to BIS 4. **Registration**: BIS issues CRS registration certificate (valid for 2 years, renewable) 5. **Marking**: Product must bear the Standard Mark for CRS (BIS Registration Mark)

- **IS 13252 (Part 1):2010/IEC 60950-1:2005**: Information Technology Equipment — Safety. Covers laptops, desktops, monitors, servers, printers, scanners, plotters, point-of-sale terminals, and UPS systems. Compulsory under CRS. - **IS/IEC 62368-1:2018**: Audio/Video, Information and Communication Technology Equipment — Safety. New unified standard replacing IS 13252 for next-generation devices.

- **IS 16333 (Part 3)**: Mobile phones — Indian language support requirements. Compulsory CRS. - **IS 16046 (Part 2):2018**: Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries for portable devices (mobiles, laptops, tablets, power banks). Compulsory under CRS. Covers safety for lithium-ion cells.

- **IS 616:2017**: Audio, Video and Similar Electronic Apparatus — Safety Requirements. Compulsory under CRS. Covers televisions, set-top boxes, DVD players, audio systems, media players. - **IS 13252 (Part 1)**: Also covers projectors and video-conferencing equipment. - **IS 302 (Part 2, Section 15)**: Microwave Ovens — safety requirements (compulsory under CRS for certain models).
- **IS 13252 (Part 1)**: Covers power adapters, AC-DC converters for IT equipment. Compulsory CRS. - **IS 16046 (Part 1):2018**: Secondary Nickel Cells and Batteries — Safety Requirements.

- **IS 15885 (Part 2/Section 13):2012**: Fixed luminaires with LED sources. Compulsory CRS. - **IS 16102 (Part 1):2012**: Self-ballasted LED lamps for general lighting — Safety. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 16102 (Part 2):2012**: Self-ballasted LED lamps — Performance. Compulsory under Scheme I.
- **IS 16242 (Part 1):2014**: Inverters and UPS up to 5 kVA (safety). Compulsory under CRS. - **IS 16242 (Part 2):2015**: Inverters and UPS — Performance and EMC requirements.
- **IS 16529**: Power Converters for use in Photovoltaic Power Generating Systems (Inverters). Compulsory CRS.
- Application fee: ₹1,000 - Registration fee: ₹1,000 - Renewal fee: ₹1,000 (every 2 years) - Testing fees: vary by product and lab (₹10,000–₹50,000 typical range)

chunks.section: Textiles — Indian Standards and BIS Certification
chunks.chunk_text: # Textiles — Indian Standards and BIS Certification

The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) publishes numerous standards for textiles and textile products. Some textile products fall under compulsory certification, especially those related to safety (e.g., protective clothing) or quality assurance for government procurement. The Textile Committee and BIS work together on standardization in this sector.

- **IS 2720:2019**: Grey Cotton Fabrics. Specifies requirements for grey cotton fabrics used in garment manufacturing. - **IS 11702:2015**: Dyed Cotton Fabrics — Specification. - **IS 1390**: Cotton Canvas (for tents, tarpaulins, and industrial use). - **IS 168:2016**: Cotton Sewing Thread — Specification.

- **IS 11284:2015**: Polyester-Cotton Blended Fabrics. - **IS 11702**: Dyed Polyester and Blended Fabrics. - **IS 12673**: Polyester Staple Fibre (Virgin). - **IS 3468**: Nylon Fabrics for parachutes and industrial applications.

- **IS 11871:2018**: Industrial Safety Gloves. Covers leather, rubber, and fabric gloves for industrial use. - **IS 6994 (Part 1):2013**: Industrial Safety Footwear. Specifies requirements for toe protection, slip resistance, and material quality. - **IS 15758:2007**: Flame Retardant Textiles — General Requirements. - **IS 1955:2002**: Fire Resistant Textile Fabrics.
- **IS 1332**: Jute Sacking — Specification. - **IS 2467**: Jute Hessian Cloth — Specification. - **IS 7205**: Coir Yarn — Specification.

- **IS 1963**: Methods of Test for Cotton Fabrics — Determination of Thread Density, Mass, and Tensile Strength. - **IS 1969**: Methods of Test for Textiles — Determination of Colour Fastness to Washing. - **IS 11056**: Determination of Fibre Composition (Quantitative Chemical Analysis). - **IS 15370**: Formaldehyde Content of Textile Fabrics.
- **IS 11625**: Care Labelling of Textiles. Specifies laundry care symbols (wash, bleach, dry, iron, professional care) that must be displayed on textile products sold in India.

Textile testing must be conducted at BIS-recognized or NABL-accredited laboratories. Key parameters tested include: 1. Tensile strength and elongation 2. Colour fastness (washing, rubbing, light, perspiration) 3. Dimensional stability (shrinkage) 4. Pilling resistance 5. Fabric count (threads per cm) 6. Chemical safety (formaldehyde, azo dyes, heavy metals) Source: Bureau of Indian Standards — https://www.bis.gov.in/ Source: Standards / Know Your Standard — https://standards.bis.gov.in/ Category: Textiles

chunks.section: Chemicals and Chemical Products — Indian Standards
chunks.chunk_text: # Chemicals and Chemical Products — Indian Standards

The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) publishes Indian Standards for a wide range of chemical products, including industrial chemicals, paints, adhesives, pesticides, fertilizers, and specialty chemicals. Some chemical products fall under compulsory certification via Quality Control Orders (QCOs).

- **IS 252:2013**: Sodium Hydroxide (Caustic Soda) — Specification. Technical and food grade. - **IS 253:2013**: Hydrochloric Acid (Muriatic Acid) — Specification. Technical grade. - **IS 264**: Sulphuric Acid — Specification. - **IS 323**: Calcium Carbide — Specification. - **IS 460**: Calcium Chloride (Technical Grade). - **IS 513:2018**: Carbon Black — Specification.

- **IS 15489:2013**: Ready Mixed Paint, Brushing, Acrylic Emulsion Based for Interior Use. - **IS 15957:2012**: Ready Mixed Paint, Brushing, Acrylic Emulsion Based for Exterior Use. - **IS 101 (Part 1 to 7)**: Methods of Test for Paints and Varnishes. Covers physical, chemical, optical, and durability testing. - **IS 2932:2016**: Enamel, Exterior (oil-based). For exterior wood and metal surfaces. - **IS 2933**: Enamels, Interior — Specification.

- **IS 526**: Synthetic Resin Adhesive for Plywood (Phenol and Amino Formaldehyde). Compulsory under Plywood QCO. - **IS 14823**: Cyanoacrylate Adhesives (Super Glue). - **IS 4835**: Polyvinyl Acetate Dispersion Based Adhesive (white glue).
- **IS 306**: Ammonium Sulphate — Specification. - **IS 10091**: Ammonium Phosphate Sulphate — Specification. - **IS 8360 (Part 1 to 4)**: Methods of Sampling and Test for Fertilizers.
- **IS 6392**: Malathion Technical — Specification. - **IS 8190**: Cypermethrin Technical — Specification.

- **IS 3400 (Parts 1 to 24)**: Methods of Test for Vulcanized Rubbers. Comprehensive testing covering tensile strength, hardness, abrasion, compression set, and ageing. - **IS 5714:2019**: Rubber Hose for LPG (Domestic Use). Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 3708**: Rubber Gloves for Electrical Purposes.

- **IS 10146:2011**: Polyethylene for Safe Use in Contact with Foodstuffs. Compulsory under QCO. - **IS 10151**: PVC and its Copolymers for Safe Use in Contact with Foodstuffs. Compulsory under QCO. - **IS 12252**: Polyethylene Water Storage Tanks. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 15328**: PVC Pipes for Water Supply — Specification.

Chemical testing must be conducted at NABL-accredited or BIS-recognized laboratories. Key tests include: 1. Purity and assay 2. Heavy metal content (lead, mercury, cadmium, arsenic) 3. pH value 4. Specific gravity 5. Viscosity 6. Flash point and flammability 7. Toxicity and environmental impact parameters Source: Bureau of Indian Standards — https://www.bis.gov.in/ Source: Standards / Know Your Standard — https://standards.bis.gov.in/ Category: Chemicals

chunks.section: Automotive Standards — Indian Standards for Vehicles and Components
chunks.chunk_text: # Automotive Standards — Indian Standards for Vehicles and Components

The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) publishes standards for automotive components and accessories. Several automotive products are under compulsory certification through Quality Control Orders issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH). BIS works in conjunction with the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and other type-approval agencies.

- **IS 4151:2015**: Protective Helmets for Two-Wheeler Riders. Compulsory under Helmet (Quality Control) Order, 2018. Mandatory testing includes impact absorption, penetration resistance, chinstrap retention, field of vision, and labelling.

- **IS 2553 (Part 1):2019**: Safety Glass for Road Transport Vehicles — Specification (Front Windshield). Compulsory under Safety Glass QCO. - **IS 2553 (Part 2):2019**: Safety Glass for Road Transport Vehicles — Specification (Side, Rear, and Roof Windows). Compulsory.

- **IS 15633:2018**: Automotive Pneumatic Tyres for Passenger Cars. Compulsory under Pneumatic Tyres and Tubes QCO. - **IS 15636:2018**: Automotive Pneumatic Tyres for Commercial Vehicles. Compulsory. - **IS 13098:2013**: Automotive Pneumatic Tyres for Two and Three Wheeled Motor Vehicles. Compulsory. - **IS 15627:2005**: Pneumatic Tyres for Agricultural Tractors.

- **IS 2062**: Hot Rolled Steel (used in automotive body/chassis manufacturing). Compulsory under Steel QCO. - **IS 1732**: Rear View Mirrors for Motor Vehicles. - **IS 10262**: Concrete Mix Proportioning (relevant for road infrastructure).

- **IS 14257:2020**: Automotive Vehicles — Storage Batteries (Lead-Acid type for starting, lighting, ignition). Referenced in Central Motor Vehicle Rules. - **IS 16046 (Part 2)**: Lithium-Ion Batteries for Electric Vehicles. Under CRS.
- **IS 10119 (Part 1)**: Motor Vehicle Headlamps — Specification. - **IS 6381**: Motor Vehicle Direction Indicators. - **IS 2552**: Reflex Reflectors for Vehicles.

- **IS 1363 (Parts 1 to 3)**: Hexagon Head Bolts, Screws, and Nuts (ISO metric). Widely used in automotive assembly. - **IS 1367 (Parts 1 to 20)**: Technical Supply Conditions for Threaded Steel Fasteners.

Automotive components under BIS certification must be tested at recognized laboratories for: 1. Impact and crash-worthiness (helmets, safety glass) 2. Road performance (tyres — speed rating, load index, endurance) 3. Environmental resistance (corrosion, temperature cycling) 4. Electrical safety (batteries, lighting) 5. Material composition (steel grade, rubber compound) Key BIS-recognized testing laboratories for automotive products include ARAI (Pune), CIRT (Pune), and ICAT (Manesar). Source: Bureau of Indian Standards — https://www.bis.gov.in/ Source: MoRTH — https://morth.nic.in/ Source: Standards / Know Your Standard — https://standards.bis.gov.in/ Category: Automotive

chunks.section: Medical Devices — Indian Standards and BIS Certification
chunks.chunk_text: # Medical Devices — Indian Standards and BIS Certification

Medical devices in India are regulated by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) under the Medical Devices Rules, 2017. BIS publishes Indian Standards for medical equipment safety, performance, and testing. The Medical Devices (Quality Control) Orders mandate BIS certification for specific categories.

- **IS 13450:2013**: Sterile, Single Use Hypodermic Syringes. Compulsory under Medical Devices QCO. Covers 1 mL to 50 mL capacity syringes. - **IS 8248:2009**: Sterile, Single Use Hypodermic Needles. Compulsory. Specifies gauge, length, sharpness, and sterility requirements. - **IS 7262:2014**: Condoms (Male Latex Rubber). Compulsory. Mandatory burst volume and pressure, freedom from holes, and tensile properties testing.

- **IS 15714:2022**: Endotracheal Tubes — Specification. - **IS 5765 (Part 2)**: Surgical Implants — General Requirements for marking, packaging, and labelling. - **IS/ISO 5832 (Parts 1 to 14)**: Implants for Surgery — Metallic Materials (stainless steel, cobalt-chromium, titanium alloys).

- **IS/IEC 60601-1:2010**: Medical Electrical Equipment — General Requirements for Basic Safety and Essential Performance. Foundational safety standard for all powered medical devices. - **IS/IEC 60601-1-2**: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements for medical equipment. - **IS 12048:2011**: Non-Invasive Blood Pressure Monitors — Requirements. - **IS 9919**: Pulse Oximeters for medical use.

- **IS 9473:2002**: Surgical Rubber Gloves — Specification. - **IS 16289:2014**: Respiratory Protective Devices — Filtering Half Masks to protect against particles (similar to N95 masks). - **IS 17423:2020**: Face Masks (General Purpose) — Requirements and Test Methods. Published during COVID-19 pandemic.
- **IS 6527**: Dental X-Ray Film and Processing Chemicals. - **IS 7840**: Dental Composite Restorative Materials.

- **IS/ISO 11135**: Sterilization of health-care products — Ethylene oxide. - **IS/ISO 11137 (Parts 1 to 3)**: Sterilization of health-care products — Radiation. - **IS/ISO 17665**: Sterilization of health-care products — Moist heat (autoclaves).

Medical device testing must be conducted at: - NABL-accredited laboratories - BIS-recognized testing laboratories - Notified laboratories under Medical Devices Rules, 2017 Key test parameters: 1. Biocompatibility (cytotoxicity, sensitization, irritation) 2. Sterility and endotoxin testing 3. Electrical safety (IS/IEC 60601-1) 4. Packaging integrity 5. Dimensional accuracy 6. Material composition and heavy metals Source: Bureau of Indian Standards — https://www.bis.gov.in/ Source: CDSCO — https://cdsco.gov.in/ Source: Standards / Know Your Standard — https://standards.bis.gov.in/ Category: Medical Devices

chunks.section: Household Products — Indian Standards and BIS Certification
chunks.chunk_text: # Household Products — Indian Standards and BIS Certification

BIS certifies numerous household products under Scheme I (ISI Mark) to ensure safety and quality for consumers. Quality Control Orders cover domestic pressure cookers, gas stoves, LPG equipment, water storage tanks, and other essential household items.

- **IS 2347:2017**: Domestic Pressure Cookers. Compulsory under Domestic Pressure Cooker (Quality Control) Order. Mandatory testing includes operating pressure (1.0 kg/cm²), burst pressure (≥4× working pressure), safety relief valve, handle strength, and gasket durability. - **IS 4246:2002**: Domestic Gas Stoves for use with LPG. Compulsory under Gas Stoves QCO. Tests include gas consumption, thermal efficiency (≥68%), flame stability, and anti-tilting. - **IS 9798**: Low Pressure Regulators for LPG mixtures. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 8468:2015**: Domestic LPG Cylinders. Compulsory under Scheme I.

- **IS 12252:2006**: Polyethylene Water Storage Tanks. Compulsory under Scheme I. Covers overhead and ground-level tanks from 100 to 10,000 litres. Mandatory food-grade polyethylene requirements. - **IS 14543:2024**: Packaged Drinking Water. Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 16240:2014**: Gravity-based Domestic Water Purifiers. Specifies performance requirements for non-electric purifiers.

- **IS 781:2019**: Waste Cocks — Specification. Covers brass, bronze, and gunmetal waste cocks for bathrooms. - **IS 2692:2015**: Ferrule Cocks. Specification for brass ferrule cocks used in plumbing. - **IS 15778:2018**: Chlorinated PVC (CPVC) Pipes for Hot and Cold Water Distribution. Compulsory. - **IS 15328:2003**: PVC Pipes for Water Supply. - **IS 2556 (Parts 1 to 3)**: Vitreous Sanitary Appliances (Wash basins, WC pans, urinals).

- **IS 4905:2017**: Padlocks — Specification. Covers pin tumbler padlocks in various security grades. - **IS 2062**: Steel used in furniture and fittings manufacturing. - **IS 13414**: Stainless Steel Utensils for Domestic Use.

- **IS 15301:2017**: Domestic Smoke Alarms. Specifies sensitivity, alarm level, and battery life. - **IS 2171:2018**: Portable Fire Extinguishers. Compulsory for commercial buildings. - **IS 2190:2010**: Selection, Installation, and Maintenance of First-Aid Fire Extinguishers.

Under the BIS Act, 2016: - All ISI-marked products must display the Standard Mark, licence number, IS number, and manufacturing date - Consumers can verify ISI licence authenticity on bis.gov.in - Complaints can be filed through BIS CARE or consumer helpline 1800-11-4000 Source: Bureau of Indian Standards — https://www.bis.gov.in/ Source: BIS CARE — https://www.bis.gov.in/index.php/consumer-affairs/consumer-complaints/ Category: Household Products

chunks.section: Mechanical and Industrial Equipment — Indian Standards
chunks.chunk_text: # Mechanical and Industrial Equipment — Indian Standards

The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) publishes extensive standards for mechanical engineering, industrial equipment, and manufacturing. These standards cover steel, fasteners, pressure vessels, bearings, welding, and industrial safety equipment.

- **IS 2062:2011**: Hot Rolled Medium and High Tensile Structural Steel. Compulsory under Steel QCO. Used in construction, bridges, pressure vessels, and shipbuilding. - **IS 1786:2008**: High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement (TMT Bars). Compulsory under Steel QCO. Grades: Fe 415, Fe 500, Fe 500D, Fe 550, Fe 600. - **IS 2830:2012**: Carbon Steel Cast Billet Ingots, Billets, Blooms and Slabs. Compulsory. - **IS 277**: Galvanized Steel Sheets (Plain and Corrugated). Compulsory under Scheme I. - **IS 10748:2004**: Hot Rolled Steel Strip for Welded Tubes and Pipes.

- **IS 1363 (Parts 1 to 3)**: Hexagon Head Bolts, Screws and Nuts (ISO Metric). - **IS 2825:1969**: Code for Unfired Pressure Vessels. - **IS 803**: Code of practice for design, fabrication and erection of vertical mild steel cylindrical welded oil storage tanks. - **IS 2585**: Portable Steel LPG Cylinders.

- **IS 16192:2014**: Rolling Bearings — Dynamic Load Ratings and Rating Life (ISO 281 adopted). - **IS 3824 (Parts 1 to 4)**: Rolling Bearings — Boundary Dimensions. - **IS 15945**: Tapered Roller Bearings — Specification.

- **IS 814:2004**: Covered Electrodes for Manual Metal Arc Welding of Carbon and Carbon-Manganese Steel. - **IS 1278**: Filler Rods and Wires for Gas Welding. - **IS 3613**: Acceptance Tests for Wire Flux Combinations for Submerged Arc Welding.

- **IS 2925:1984**: Industrial Safety Helmets. - **IS 5983:2020**: Eye Protectors (Industrial Safety Goggles). - **IS 6994 (Part 1 to 3)**: Industrial Safety Footwear. - **IS 3521**: Industrial Safety Belts and Harnesses.

- **IS 778:2019**: Specification for copper alloy gate, globe and check valves. - **IS 1239 (Parts 1 to 2)**: Steel Tubes, Tubulars and Other Wrought Steel Fittings. - **IS 2062**: Steel flanges for pipes, valves, and fittings. chunks.section: Construction and Building Materials — Indian Standards and BIS Certification
chunks.chunk_text: # Construction and Building Materials — Indian Standards and BIS Certification

Building materials are heavily regulated by BIS through Quality Control Orders. Cement, steel, and structural materials are under compulsory BIS certification. Standards are developed by BIS committees in conjunction with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Indian Roads Congress (IRC).

- **IS 269:2015**: Ordinary Portland Cement — 33, 43, and 53 grades. Compulsory under Cement QCO. - **IS 1489 (Part 1):2015**: Portland Pozzolana Cement (Fly-ash based). Compulsory. - **IS 1489 (Part 2):2015**: Portland Pozzolana Cement (Calcined clay based). Compulsory. - **IS 455:2015**: Portland Slag Cement. Compulsory. - **IS 8112:2013**: OPC 43 Grade. Compulsory. Most commonly used for general construction. - **IS 12269:2013**: OPC 53 Grade. Compulsory. Used for high-strength concrete and pre-stressed concrete. - **IS 3466:1988**: Masonry Cement. Compulsory. - **IS 12330:1988**: Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement. Compulsory. - **IS 16415:2015**: Composite Cement. Compulsory.

- **IS 456:2000**: Plain and Reinforced Concrete — Code of Practice. The foundational standard for structural concrete design in India. - **IS 10262:2019**: Concrete Mix Proportioning — Guidelines. - **IS 516:2018**: Method of Tests for Strength of Concrete (compressive, flexural, split tensile). - **IS 383:2016**: Coarse and Fine Aggregates for Concrete. Specifies grading, deleterious materials limits, and physical property requirements.

- **IS 1077:2019**: Common Burnt Clay Building Bricks. Specifies compressive strength classes (3.5 to 40 MPa), water absorption, and efflorescence. - **IS 2185 (Part 1):2005**: Concrete Masonry Units — Hollow and Solid. Specifies load-bearing and non-load-bearing blocks. - **IS 3952:1988**: Burnt Clay Hollow Blocks. - **IS 12894:2002**: Fly Ash Lime Bricks.

- **IS 303:2018**: Plywood for General Purposes. Compulsory under Plywood QCO. - **IS 710:2010**: Marine Grade Plywood. Compulsory under Plywood QCO. - **IS 848:2006**: Specifications for Synthetic Resin Adhesives for Construction. - **IS 12406:2003**: Medium Density Fibre Board (MDF).
- **IS 13630 (Part 1 to 14)**: Ceramic Tiles — Testing methods. - **IS 15622:2017**: Ceramic Floor Tiles (Pressed, Dry Process). Compulsory under Tiles QCO. - **IS 13712:1993**: Vitrified Tiles.
- **IS 2062:2011**: Hot Rolled Structural Steel. Compulsory. - **IS 1786:2008**: TMT Bars. Compulsory.

- **IS 3384:2016**: Bitumen Primer. - **IS 1580:2012**: Bituminous Compound for Waterproofing and Damp-Proofing. Source: Bureau of Indian Standards — https://www.bis.gov.in/ Source: Standards / Know Your Standard — https://standards.bis.gov.in/ Category: Construction and Building Materials

chunks.section: BIS General Information — Organization, Services, and Consumer Resources
chunks.chunk_text: # BIS General Information — Organization, Services, and Consumer Resources

chunks.section: About the Bureau of Indian Standards
chunks.chunk_text: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is the National Standards Body of India, established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. BIS operates under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution. BIS headquarters are located in Manak Bhavan, 9 Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, New Delhi — 110002.

1. **Standards Formulation**: BIS formulates Indian Standards through Technical Committees comprising representatives from industry, government, consumer organizations, and technical institutions. As of 2024, BIS has published over 22,000 Indian Standards across 14 sectors. 2. **Product Certification (Conformity Assessment)**: BIS operates multiple certification schemes: - **Scheme I (ISI Mark)**: For products under compulsory or voluntary certification. Requires factory inspection, testing at BIS-recognized labs, and continuous surveillance. - **Scheme II (CRS)**: Compulsory Registration Scheme for electronics and IT goods. No factory inspection required. - **Scheme IV (CoC)**: Certificate of Conformity for imported goods. Ensures imported products meet Indian Standards. - **Scheme V (SMIS)**: Standard Mark for Indian Standards for import goods. - **Scheme X (FMCS)**: Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme for overseas manufacturers. 3. **Hallmarking**: BIS operates the hallmarking scheme for gold and silver jewellery to certify purity. 4. **Laboratory Services**: BIS recognizes testing laboratories under the Laboratory Recognition Scheme (LRS) and operates the LIMS portal. 5. **Standards Promotion**: Through Standards Clubs, BIS promotes awareness of standardization among students and industry. 6. **Training**: BIS provides training programs on standardization, quality management, and conformity assessment.

chunks.section: How to Apply for BIS Certification
chunks.chunk_text: ### Scheme I (ISI Mark) Application Process 1. **Step 1**: Visit manakonline.in and register 2. **Step 2**: Select the relevant Indian Standard and product category 3. **Step 3**: Upload required documents: - Factory layout plan - Manufacturing process details - List of testing equipment - Quality control procedures - Previous test reports (if any) 4. **Step 4**: Pay the application fee online 5. **Step 5**: BIS officer conducts factory inspection 6. **Step 6**: Product samples collected for testing at BIS-recognized lab 7. **Step 7**: If tests pass and factory complies, licence is granted 8. **Step 8**: Licence is valid until cancelled or suspended; annual marking fee and surveillance continue ### Fees (Indicative, subject to revision) - Application fee: ₹1,000 - Annual marking fee: Based on annual production value (minimum ₹1,000 to maximum ₹5,00,000) - Testing fee: Varies by product and laboratory

chunks.section: Simplified Procedure for Grant of Licence
chunks.chunk_text: BIS has introduced a Simplified Procedure for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to obtain ISI certification faster. Under this procedure: - Reduced documentation requirements - Expedited factory inspection - Lower testing fees for first-time applicants - Online tracking of application status - Faster processing (target: 60 days for MSME applications)

Consumers who suspect a product bearing the ISI Mark or BIS Registration Mark is of substandard quality can: 1. File a complaint online at https://www.bis.gov.in/consumer-affairs/ 2. Call BIS CARE helpline: 1800-11-4000 (toll-free) 3. Email: biscare@bis.gov.in 4. Visit the nearest BIS Branch Office BIS investigates complaints, can draw product samples for testing, and take enforcement action including licence cancellation.

BIS has 5 Regional Offices and 38 Branch Offices across India: - **Northern Region**: Delhi (HQ), Chandigarh, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Jammu, Patna - **Southern Region**: Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Thiruvananthapuram, Kochi, Visakhapatnam - **Eastern Region**: Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Ranchi - **Western Region**: Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune, Bhopal, Nagpur, Rajkot - **Central Office**: New Delhi — Manak Bhavan

- **Main website**: https://www.bis.gov.in/ - **Standards portal**: https://standards.bis.gov.in/ - **Manak Online (e-BIS)**: https://manakonline.in/ — For licence applications, renewals, and tracking - **LIMS portal**: https://lims.bis.gov.in/ — Laboratory Information Management System - **Know Your Standard**: https://www.bis.gov.in/know-your-standard/ - **Standards Store**: https://www.services.bis.gov.in:8071/php/BIS_2.0/dgms/default Source: Bureau of Indian Standards — https://www.bis.gov.in/ Source: BIS Act, 2016 — https://www.bis.gov.in/index.php/the-bureau/act-rules-regulations/ Category: General BIS Information
